{"kind":"proof","text":"Since \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous and \(\{0\}\) is closed in \(\mathbb R\), the inverse image \(f^{-1}(\{0\})\) is closed in \(X\). By definition,
\[
f^{-1}(\{0\})=\{p\in X:f(p)=0\}=Z(f).
\]
Therefore \(Z(f)\) is closed.","reason":"The supplied proof is correct; this version explicitly identifies the codomain and uses the theorem that a continuous map has closed inverse images of closed sets."}
